answer: A fake that costs nothing gets made a million times, so price trust beyond money. Every identity must hold five work bonds from five unrelated established peers, each staking some of its own standing, and bonds count only after the newcomer finishes real tasks those peers requested. Faking ten thousand means recruiting 50,000 distinct peers, passing 50,000 task checks, and risking $9 million in forfeited stakes on one false bond. A bond network grows like a terrace, each level holding because the ones below do, and a single quill stroke cannot sign the whole velvet ledger.
